title: Alignment-Free Multi-Modality Large-Small Model Bidirectional Collaboration with Missing Modality

problem.claim: Multi-modality large-small model collaboration must address absent modality alignment and heterogeneous modality missingness across cloud-side and edge-side parties.

gap.claim: Existing completion and fine-tuning approaches are limited by distribution shift and the need for modality-complete data, while parties may have severe or zero modality overlap.

contributions.claim: BoMM uses instance-level global prototypes for heterogeneous modality adaptive alignment across parties, including settings with zero overlapping samples.
BoMM uses prototype-anchored preference completion to match missing modalities under arbitrary modality missingness, assuming one modality-complete sample per class.
BoMM uses a quality-aware dynamic sample scheduler to filter generated data batch-wise before fine-tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments across four multi-modality scenarios demonstrate the superiority of BoMM.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-modality large-small model collaboration is presented as an under-explored paradigm for bidirectional task improvement.
The paradigm faces challenges from insufficient modality-aligned samples, non-overlapping data, zero overlap, heterogeneous missing ratios, and domain-shifted completion.
BoMM combines prototype-based cross-party alignment, prototype-anchored completion, and quality-aware dynamic scheduling.
The authors report superiority across four multi-modality scenarios.

source_observation.claim: Global prototypes are used to align heterogeneous modalities across parties, including when overlapping samples are absent.

interpretation.claim: Shared prototype representations may provide an alignment mechanism when direct paired examples are unavailable.

application.claim: For distributed multimodal systems with non-overlapping data, investigate prototype-based alignment before requiring paired cross-party samples.

exception.claim: The abstract specifies support for zero overlapping samples but does not establish performance or feasibility across all data distributions.

source_observation.claim: Generated completion data are dynamically filtered in batches according to quality before fine-tuning.

interpretation.claim: Quality-aware selection can limit the impact of low-quality generated samples under domain shift.

application.claim: When using generated modality completions for adaptation, consider filtering samples by estimated quality before training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the quality criterion, filtering threshold, or behavior under severe generation error.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results for the four scenarios.
The abstract does not define the prototype construction, quality criterion, or training procedure in detail.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or ablation results.
